evidence_placement.note: Evidence is attributed to a race by following the rows that cite it, then the artifact those rows share, then other captures of the same URL. An artifact serving more than one race — the season calendars serve 124 — is placed to none, so these totals do not add up to the whole and are not meant to.

manifest.attribution: Race names, dates, UCI classes and cancellations for the season calendar are derived from the English Wikipedia articles '2026 UCI World Tour', '2026 UCI Women's World Tour' and '2026 UCI ProSeries', licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

season.note: Victories in the races this project holds a result for, not in the season. A win in a race held at CALENDAR depth is invisible here because nothing in this database records it. Names are counted as published: two spellings of one squad stay two, because a rule that merged them would as readily merge two squads that differ.

freshness_legend.means: The race has not happened yet.
The race is under way as of the date the evidence is current to.
The race has finished and a result is held for every stage.
The race has finished and a result is held for some of it.
The race has finished, no result is held, and the pipeline has fetched something for it since it finished. The absence is a gap being worked.
The race has finished, no result is held, and nothing has been fetched for it since it finished. Nobody has looked.
The race was cancelled, so no result will ever exist.
No start date is held, so nothing about timing can be judged.
The database holds no observation at all, so there is no date to be current to.

manifest.freshness_note: Every race carries a `freshness` block: the date its evidence is current to, the date anything was last fetched for it, the date the schedule next looks, and the state of its result. This index carries the part a race list renders; the counters behind it — how many looks were answered, refused or failed, how many committed capture targets name the race, how many gaps are open — are on the race's own chunk at `race/<slug>.json`, because they are what a reader of one race asks and this file is fetched by everyone. `capture_targets: 0` there means the schedule has no address for that race and no recheck date can cause anything to be fetched for it. A key absent from a freshness block is a fact not held, which is why nulls are not written. All dates are judged against the newest observation in the vault, never against the reader's clock — this is a schedule, not a live feed, and the freshest anything here can be is the last run that succeeded. `freshness_as_of` is that date, stated once because it is a property of this bundle rather than of any race.
